title: Faithful flatness of finite-type algebraic-to-analytic local rings

items.title: Common completions of algebraic and holomorphic local rings and their finite-type quotients
items.design_state: No design section governed this pair; local finite-jet comparison is proved from inspected full-text sources and current mathematical suppliers.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix an integer $n\ge1$, put
$P=\mathbb C[w_1,\ldots,w_n]$, and let $\mathfrak m=(w_1,\ldots,w_n)$.
Let $A_0=P_{\mathfrak m}$ be the localization at the polynomials nonzero at
the origin, let $H=\mathbb C\{w_1,\ldots,w_n\}$ be the ring of holomorphic
function germs at the origin, and let $T$ be the set of coefficient arrays
$a=(a_\alpha)_{\alpha\in\mathbb N^n}\in\mathbb C^{\mathbb N^n}$, written
$\sum_\alpha a_\alpha w^\alpha$ where $w^\alpha=\prod_{i=1}^n w_i^{\alpha_i}$,
with pointwise addition and multiplication
defined by $(ab)_\alpha=\sum_{\beta+\gamma=\alpha}a_\beta b_\gamma$. These
operations make $T$ a commutative unital ring: each convolution is finite, its
multiplicative identity has coefficient $1$ at $\alpha=0$ and $0$ elsewhere,
and no convergence condition is imposed; this
ring is denoted $\mathbb C\llbracket w_1,\ldots,w_n\rrbracket$. For
each polynomial in $P$, its finitely supported coefficient array defines the
canonical ring map $P\to T$; for an ideal $I\subseteq P$, $IT$ denotes the ideal
of $T$ generated by its image under this map. For any finitely generated ideal
$I\subseteq
\mathfrak m$, set $A_I=A_0/IA_0$ and $H_I=H/IH$. For a local ring $R$ with
maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_R$, define its completion by
$\widehat R=\varprojlim_{k\ge1}R/\mathfrak m_R^k$.

The polynomial-to-germ map induces a local homomorphism $A_I\to H_I$. The
four rings $A_0,H,A_I,H_I$ are Noetherian local rings, and the induced map on
completions identifies both $\widehat{A_I}$ and $\widehat{H_I}$ canonically
with $T/IT$. In particular, the comparison uses the same extended defining
ideal $I$ and does not replace it by its radical, so nilpotent classes are
retained.
items.axiom_base: ZF + AC, as required by the finite-quotient completion supplier.

references.title: Jean-Pierre Serre, Géométrie algébrique et géométrie analytique, §2, no. 6 and Annex §§22–24
Johannes Anschütz, Lecture Notes on Étale Cohomology, §§3.24–3.26
Kiran S. Kedlaya, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.726, Lecture 22: GAGA

items.proof_obligation: Identify polynomial and convergent finite jets, pass to the two ambient completions, and extend the same finite defining ideal without radicalization.
items.strategy: Identify each algebraic and analytic quotient modulo the k-th maximal-ideal power with the same truncated polynomial ring; then take inverse limits and apply finite-quotient completion.

items.title: Faithful flatness of finite-type algebraic-to-analytic local rings
items.design_state: No design section governed this pair; complete conditional proof uses the local completion lemma and inspected flatness sources.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $X$ be a scheme of finite type over $\mathbb C$
and let $x\in X$ be a closed point with residue field $\mathbb C$. Choose an
affine neighborhood of $x$ presented as (adding a dummy coordinate if needed)
$\operatorname{Spec}(\mathbb C[w_1,\ldots,w_n]/I)$, with $n\ge1$, $I$ a
finitely generated polynomial ideal contained in $(w_1,\ldots,w_n)$, and $x$
the origin. Write
$A=(\mathbb C[w_1,\ldots,w_n]_{(w_1,\ldots,w_n)})/I\mathbb C[w_1,\ldots,w_n]_{(w_1,\ldots,w_n)}$.
On this chart, define the analytic local ring by extending the same ideal to
holomorphic germs,
$B=\mathbb C\{w_1,\ldots,w_n\}/I\mathbb C\{w_1,\ldots,w_n\}$; this quotient
retains the given scheme structure, including nilpotents. For a local ring $R$
with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_R$, let
$\widehat R=\varprojlim_{k\ge1}R/\mathfrak m_R^k$.

The canonical local homomorphism $A\to B$, which sends each polynomial class
to the same holomorphic germ, is injective and faithfully flat.
Its induced map $\widehat A\to\widehat B$ is an isomorphism, with both
completions canonically identified with
$\mathbb C\llbracket w_1,\ldots,w_n\rrbracket/I\mathbb C\llbracket w_1,\ldots,w_n\rrbracket$. For every
$A$-module $M$, the map $M\to M\otimes_A B$ is injective, and the quotient
$B/A$ is a flat $A$-module. These are local-ring conclusions; no relative
direct-image comparison is asserted.
items.axiom_base: ZF + full AC; AC supplies the completion and faithful-flatness hypotheses and implies DC for the supplied Tor results.

references.title: Jean-Pierre Serre, Géométrie algébrique et géométrie analytique, §2, no. 6 and Annex §§22–24
Johannes Anschütz, Lecture Notes on Étale Cohomology, §§3.24–3.26
Kiran S. Kedlaya, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.726, Lecture 22: GAGA

items.proof_obligation: Descend flatness from the common Noetherian local completion, prove local faithful flatness by the proper-ideal criterion, and use the right-module Tor sequence to prove flatness of B/A; carry AC and the derived DC condition explicitly.
items.strategy: Use the common completion to descend flatness, then prove local faithfulness, tensor-unit injectivity, and B/A flatness.

title: Faithful flatness of finite-type algebraic-to-analytic local rings — Examples

items.title: Unequal local rings with equal completions
items.design_state: No design section governed this pair; source-informed example verified with a local nonrationality argument.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $A=\mathbb C[t]_{(t)}$ be the localization of
$\mathbb C[t]$ at polynomials nonzero at $0$, and let $B=\mathbb C\{t\}$ be
the ring of holomorphic germs at $0$. The canonical map $A\to B$ is faithfully
flat and induces the common completion $\mathbb C\llbracket t\rrbracket$, but it is not
surjective: the convergent exponential germ
$e(t)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}t^n/n!$ is not in its image.
items.axiom_base: ZF + AC, inherited from the faithful-flatness theorem.

references.title: Jean-Pierre Serre, Géométrie algébrique et géométrie analytique, §2, no. 6 and Annex §§22–24
Johannes Anschütz, Lecture Notes on Étale Cohomology, §§3.24–3.26
Kiran S. Kedlaya, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.726, Lecture 22: GAGA

items.proof_obligation: Prove that the exponential germ is not rational by comparing its coefficients with every p/q representation whose denominator is nonzero at the origin.

items.title: Faithful flatness retaining a nilpotent class
items.design_state: No design section governed this pair; the completion comparison is checked without replacing the nonreduced ideal by its radical.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $X=\operatorname{Spec}(\mathbb C[x,y]/(x^2))$
and let $p$ be the closed $\mathbb C$-point at the origin. Write
$T=\mathbb C^{\mathbb N^2}$ for the ring of coefficient arrays
$(a_{i,j})_{i,j\ge0}$, with pointwise addition and finite Cauchy multiplication
$(ab)_{i,j}=\sum_{r=0}^i\sum_{s=0}^j a_{r,s}b_{i-r,j-s}$; this formal ring is
denoted $\mathbb C\llbracket x,y\rrbracket$, with $x$ and $y$ the arrays
supported at $(1,0)$ and $(0,1)$, respectively, and its unit is supported at
$(0,0)$ with coefficient $1$. No convergence condition is imposed. Its
algebraic local ring is
$A=(\mathbb C[x,y]/(x^2))_{(x,y)}$, and its analytic local ring is
$B=\mathbb C\{x,y\}/(x^2)$. The canonical map $A\to B$ is faithfully flat
with common maximal-ideal completion $T/(x^2T)$, and the class of $x$ is a
nonzero element whose square is zero in both rings.
items.axiom_base: ZF + AC, inherited from the faithful-flatness theorem.

references.title: Jean-Pierre Serre, Géométrie algébrique et géométrie analytique, §2, no. 6 and Annex §§22–24

Kiran S. Kedlaya, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.726, Lecture 22: GAGA

items.proof_obligation: Use the common formal completion to show the class x remains nonzero; the quotient definition gives x^2=0 in both local rings.
